source_name: EPC List of SEPA Scheme Countries (EPC409-09)
why_relevant: Versioned authoritative list defining which countries/territories are in SEPA geographical scope; the version history is a clean machine-trackable record of Montenegro's status change.

source_name: EPC Register of Participants (SEPA scheme adherence database)
why_relevant: Institution-level ground truth: which Montenegrin PSPs adhere to SCT, SCT Inst, SDD and when. Enables counting Montenegrin SEPA participants over time — a hard quantitative indicator of payments-market integration.

source_name: EEAS / EU Delegation to Montenegro — payments & SEPA statements
why_relevant: EU Delegation publishes the political framing and donor-programme announcements around SEPA inclusion and Growth Plan disbursements; useful for dating commitments and identifying funded projects.

source_name: EC Growth Plan / Reform and Growth Facility for the Western Balkans — Montenegro Reform Agenda
why_relevant: The Reform Agenda ties EU disbursements to dated reform steps; payments-related steps (SEPA, digitalisation of payments, financial-sector reform) appear as conditioned, monitored milestones with payment-request assessments — forward-looking targets plus audit trail.

source_name: Western Balkans Investment Framework (WBIF) project database
why_relevant: Searchable database of EU/IFI-funded technical assistance and investment projects in Montenegro, including 'Digital future' and private-sector windows; identifies who is funding payments/digital-finance modernisation and with what deliverables.

source_name: EBRD Transition Report — Montenegro country assessment
why_relevant: Annual EBRD country assessment with transition-quality scores covering financial-sector depth and digitalisation; explicitly notes SEPA integration. Provides cross-country benchmarking for Montenegro's payments market.

source_name: EBRD Montenegro Country Diagnostic — Private investment challenges and opportunities
why_relevant: Structural diagnostic of Montenegro's private and financial sector; the diagnostic series (see Serbia/North Macedonia peers) covers access to finance, banking-sector structure and digitalisation constraints relevant to payments/POS adoption.

source_name: EBRD Montenegro country strategy & project/news pages
why_relevant: Country strategy documents and project announcements reveal EBRD-financed financial-sector and 'Go Digital in the Western Balkans' operations with local banks (e.g. Addiko, CKB) — indirect evidence of where payments/digital-finance capacity is being built.

source_name: IMF Article IV Consultation — Montenegro (staff reports and concluding statements)
why_relevant: Annual macro-financial surveillance covering banking-sector structure, euroisation, financial stability and central-bank independence; frames EU-accession-driven financial-sector reform (2028 accession target). Contains benchmarked statistics not published domestically in comparable form.

source_name: Banca d'Italia — TIPS Clone for Western Balkans (project communications)
why_relevant: Banca d'Italia, with ECB/Eurosystem backing, supplies the TIPS-clone instant-payment platform to Montenegro and peers under a Jan-2025 Rome agreement; its releases carry onboarding dates, participant scope and the regional roll-out calendar (second window Nov 2026) — infrastructure facts no domestic publisher produces.

source_name: ECB — Governing Council decisions and MIP news on non-euro-area/Western Balkans TIPS access
why_relevant: The 7 June 2024 Governing Council decision authorising the TIPS clone for Montenegro, Kosovo, North Macedonia, BiH and Albania is the formal regulatory approval underpinning the instant-payments agenda; ECB MIP news and speeches add cross-border payments strategy context.

source_name: Central Bank of Montenegro (CBCG) — SEPA / EU-integration press releases (bilingual me/en)
why_relevant: CBCG leads the Chapter 4 negotiating working group and is the national counterpart to EPC/ECB/Banca d'Italia. Its releases carry accession-linked payment facts and quantified claims (e.g. estimated combined SEPA + TIPS-clone benefit ~2.3% of GDP) and its commentary on EC reports flags how the EC assesses CBCG activity.

source_name: Skupština Crne Gore (Parliament) — EU accession section and payment-law adoption records
why_relevant: Dates and texts of the accession-driven payment legislation (Zakon o platnom prometu amendments aligned to PSD2, adopted 29 Sep 2022; later SEPA/DORA-aligned amendments). Legislative record is the audit trail behind the EC/EPC assessments.

source_name: European Western Balkans (analytical outlet) — SEPA / payments accession coverage
why_relevant: Specialist enlargement outlet that tracks and contextualises SEPA/EU-payments steps across all six WB economies; useful as a regional cross-check and for surfacing documents that official portals bury.

source_name: CEE Legal Matters briefing — 'SEPA in Montenegro: Benefits and Challenges'
why_relevant: Practitioner legal briefing dating the SEPA adherence steps of Montenegrin banks (all banks approved by 13 June 2025; operational use from 6 Oct 2025) — useful corroboration of the EPC register timeline from a professional-services vantage point.

source_name: CBCG — Radne studije (Central Bank of Montenegro Working Paper series)
why_relevant: The central bank's own research department (Sektor za istraživanja i statistiku) publishes analytical working papers as free PDFs. Series confirmed to include financial-market, banking-sector, COVID-19 banking and credit/deposit analyses; the natural home for any CBCG analysis of payment habits, card usage or cash demand that is not in statistical releases.

source_name: CBCG Radna studija br. 10 — Analiza finansijskog tržišta u Crnoj Gori (PDF exemplar)
why_relevant: Concrete exemplar of the CBCG working-paper PDF pattern; useful to pin the URL template (/slike_i_fajlovi/fajlovi/fajlovi_publikacije/radne_studije/<slug>.pdf) for systematic harvesting of the whole series.

source_name: Montenegrin Journal of Economics (MNJE) — ELIT, Podgorica
why_relevant: Peer-reviewed, Scopus-indexed (Q1 SJR reported) open-access economics journal published from Podgorica by NGO 'Economic Laboratory for Transition Research' (ELIT). Regional venue where Montenegrin and Western-Balkan authors publish empirical banking, fintech-adoption and payment-behaviour studies with survey microdata.

source_name: DOAJ listing for Montenegrin Journal of Economics (metadata pointer)
why_relevant: Machine-readable article metadata/abstract feed for MNJE, letting keyword monitoring run without scraping the journal site.

source_name: Univerzitet Crne Gore — Ekonomski fakultet Podgorica (Faculty of Economics)
why_relevant: Oldest and largest Montenegrin economics faculty; staff research, conference proceedings and student/staff theses are the main domestic academic producer of survey-based work on payment behaviour and banking. Faculty pages carry announcements, projects and publication lists.

source_name: UCG institutional repository / 'skladiste' document store (theses and dissertations)
why_relevant: University of Montenegro hosts full-text doctoral dissertations and master theses as PDFs under /skladiste/. Confirmed to host at least one banking/finance dissertation (Đurović, on national development and financial institutions). Theses frequently contain original merchant/consumer surveys and reconstructed card/POS series unavailable elsewhere.

source_name: ISSP — Institut za strateške studije i projekcije (Institute for Strategic Studies and Prognoses), Podgorica
why_relevant: Montenegro's best-known independent economic think tank; runs its own recurring surveys, built the macroeconomic model of Montenegro, and its researchers comment publicly on bank interest rates and financial sector conditions. Has a downloadable publications section.

source_name: DeFacto Consultancy (Podgorica) — market research and public-opinion agency
why_relevant: Described as the largest Montenegrin market-research and public-opinion agency; the most likely domestic fieldwork contractor behind bank/card/consumer-payment surveys (client-commissioned, occasionally published or press-released). Key actor to track for survey existence even when microdata is proprietary.
